title: Helping your working developer last longer

posts.topic_title: Helping your working developer last longer
posts.author: MichaelH
posts.post_subject: Helping your working developer last longer
posts.content_md:
Similar to Tom [over here](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=2132), I've been using tupperware and locking containers for a while and just started using a combination of that and Wine Savers to make my working developer last longer.

In a nutshell, cut a hole in the top of your container and glue a wine saver stopper into the hole. Now you can use the pump to remove a lot of the air inside the container and your working developer will last longer before you have to throw it out.

More details on:

[http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/archives ... er-tm.html](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/archives/238-Developer-Saver-tm.html)

I've tried using those but the cans I've found are expensive and don't have have any indicators to show how much gas remains. Until they run out and then it's pretty easy to tell 

So far the pumps always work. I've been using them for my developers and they last a good long time with the air evacuated.

posts.topic_title: Helping your working developer last longer
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Helping your working developer last longer
posts.content_md:
Did the cans work? 

If so then a large operation could buy bulk gas. There is a lot of Nitrogen in a large cylinder but it would take a lot of developer savings to pay for it. The cylinder is about $200 and it costs about $30 to fill then you would need a regulator for about $120. So for $350 you could throw our a lot of developer. However when you are runnning a roll of film a week it would start to make sense.
